long_biography.plain_text:
Saving part of Haarlem's Spaarnekerk helped set the direction of Luigi Prins's career. After working at estate agencies and spending time in Brazil, he established Cobraspen in 1984. Rather than treating ageing structures only as demolition sites, he built a regional development practice around reusing monuments and industrial buildings for new commercial purposes.

That approach later shaped projects such as SugarCity and the completion of Landhuis Elswout, which became the group's headquarters. Prins combined redevelopment with longer-term investment and operation, including office, residential and hospitality concepts. He remains the company's owner and director. His father's property career supplied relevant industry exposure, while Prins founded and built Cobraspen as a separate enterprise. Buildings and portfolio assets remain held by the business or project entities rather than by him individually.
